blogs.title: When a Dog Bite Turns Deadly – Recognizing Sepsis‑Triggered CM‑HUS in the ED
blogs.description: This post walks clinicians through the classic yet ominous presentation of Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis, the subtle shift from DIC to microangiopathic hemolysis, and the key bedside clues that should make you think of complement‑mediated TMA before the first platelets drop.

blogs.title: The ‘Hidden’ Haemolytic Episode: Why Severe Diarrhoea, Shock, and Kidney Failure Are Not the Whole Story
blogs.description: We dissect the diagnostic maze: how pancytopenia, lactic acidosis, and anuria can mask MAHA, the pitfalls of early labs (normal haptoglobin, negative Shiga toxin), and a step‑by‑step guide to ruling out TTP and STEC‑HUS while the patient’s picture evolves.

blogs.title: Complement‑Triggered TMA in the ICU – When to Pull the Plasmatic ‘Cut‑off’ and Start Eculizumab
blogs.description: Focusing on timing, this article reviews the evidence for early eculizumab in CM‑HUS, the role of plasma exchange as a bridge, and the nuanced decision‑making when active bacteraemia is still present. We also cover vaccination and prophylaxis protocols.

blogs.title: Capnocytophaga canimorsus: The Silent Instigator of a Catastrophic TMA
blogs.description: A focused case‑study on the microbiology and immunology of C. canimorsus – why it’s fastidious, how it activates complement, and why even an immunocompetent host can spiral into CM‑HUS. Includes a quick‑reference table of rare zoonotic triggers of TMA.

blogs.title: Kidney Biopsy in the Setting of Sepsis‑Associated TMA – What the Pathologist Says
blogs.description: Using this case’s biopsy images, we translate histology into clinical action: distinguishing acute tubular necrosis, thrombotic microangiopathy, and crescentic disease; interpreting immunofluorescence patterns; and explaining why a negative immune‑complex deposit steers diagnosis toward complement‑mediated disease.

blogs.title: Balancing Infection and Immunosuppression: Practical Rules for Eculizumab in Encapsulated Bacterial Sepsis
blogs.description: A pragmatic guide that outlines the infection risks of complement blockade, the timing of empirical antibiotics versus complement inhibitors, the importance of meningococcal and other vaccines, and surveillance strategies for patients who develop CM‑HUS during or after sepsis.
